label: W6-8
reason: Wave 6 stage 2: no invariant yet; the obstacle is now specific. Each block is a six-state transducer (A-F = (gap, parity)). Halting in the body needs an R to reach a fresh gap-1 odd block F. In the real run every F has a gap-3 right neighbour and every E a gap-2 one, and a gap-3 block never sends R, so F is safe while this pairing holds. It breaks only if a later phase defect catches the F before F's first N: the small-refill halts of stage 1 are exactly that. Refill fuzz with refills >= 24+r never breaks it. Window languages (k = 7, 10) neither close nor fail; the invariant needs a non-local timing comparison between each F and the next defect.
claim_note: Sheet note by nerdyjoe (Results row 24: 'Code. Binary counting + bouncing') is an analysis note with no status; no Discord mention. Drop if Dennis says it is nerdyjoe's.
next_goal: If funded: a right-to-left automaton over the six-state chain that carries, for each pending F or live wave, the digits up to the next defect (cut off where the defect provably arrives late), with size classes only in the last 2-3 blocks; check closure with a winfix4-style product search.
confidence_note: Medium-high that it never halts (exact rules, no halt to 4e9 steps, robust to fuel and block fuzz, refills >= 24+r never break the F pairing). Low that one more 2 h stage closes a proof: the needed invariant is a timing property between travelling defects, not a local one, and a Coq proof would follow as a separate multi-stage effort.
